L34: 
L35: #### Trust
L36: 
L37: We believe trust is the foundation of our relationship with pet owners. We are committed to earning your trust by providing exceptional veterinary care and open communication throughout your pet’s treatment journey.
L38: 
L39: 
L40: 
L41: #### EMpathy
L42: 
L43: We know that empathy can make all the difference in a pet’s recovery journey. That’s why we approach every case with sensitivity, compassion, and an unwavering commitment to providing personalized care.
L44: 
L45: 
L46: #### Expertise
L47: 
L48: Expertise goes beyond book knowledge or technical skills; it also requires experience working with pets facing complex medical conditions like cancer. At the Animal Cancer and Referral Center, our team has years of experience treating pets with cancer using advanced diagnostic tools and comprehensive treatment plans tailored to each patient’s needs.
L49: 
L50: 
L51: #### HOPE
L52: At the Animal Cancer and Referral Center, we believe that hope is a vital element in the journey towards healing. Our compassionate team works tirelessly to provide cutting-edge treatments and personalized care plans for your cherished pets. We understand the emotional weight that comes with a cancer diagnosis, and we strive to offer a beacon of hope through our commitment to innovative therapies and unwavering support.
L53: By placing your trust in our expertise and dedication, you can rest assured that we will stand by your side, working together to give your companions the best possible chance for the best outcomes in their cancer diagnosis.

L37: # Targeted Therapy
L38: ### What is Targeted Therapy?
L39: 
L40: The aim of targeted therapy is to attack a certain target on cancer cells while doing less damage to the normal cells in the body. Targeted drugs can be used as the primary treatment for some cancers, but are more often used in combination with surgery, radiation therapy and standard chemotherapy.
L41: There are many different types of targeted therapies available to treat people with a variety of cancers There are a few options available for our companion animals. The two main groups of these therapies include monoclonal antibodies (see lmmunotherapy section) and small molecule inhibitors, such as Palladia and Apoquel.
L42: Palladia® (toceranib phosphate) is FDA-approved for dogs with grade II or Ill recurrent cutaneous mast cell cancer with or without regional lymph node involvement. Palladia is a multiple tyrosine kinase inhibitors, having both direct antitumor and anti-angiogenic activity. Palladia is also used off-label to treat a variety of other tumors in both dogs and cats, and is used most often for neuroendocrine carcinomas.
L43: Palladia is generally well tolerated but can cause side effects such as loss of appetite, nausea/vomiting, diarrhea, low white blood cell counts and protein loss through the kidneys. Palladia can be used as a single agent in a treatment protocol, but it can also be combined with radiation therapy and standard chemotherapy. To see if Palladia is a treatment option for your pet, ask your oncologist.
L44: Apoquel is a JAK-1 inhibitor and is often used for itchy dogs. This is a product that your general veterinarian would use for seasonal skin allergies/pruritis.
L45: 
L46: lmatinib is a product that was the first product used for chronic myelogenous leukemia against the BCR/ ABL mutation that has recently come off patent and is affordable for dogs and cats. It has use against vaccine associated sarcomas and cats and mast cell tumors in dogs.
